title: Integrated Photoacoustic Ophthalmoscopy and Spectral-domain Optical Coherence Tomography
protocol: Configure the Nd:YAG laser to emit at 20 μJ/pulse with a pulse duration of 2 nsec.
Frequency-double the output laser from 1064 nm to 532 nm using a BBO crystal.
Split the 532 nm light and deliver it through a single-mode optical fiber.
Record the 1064 nm laser by a photodiode, which triggers PA signal acquisition.
Deliver the laser light onto the retina via a galvanometer and telescope configuration.
Place an unfocused needle transducer in contact with the animal's eyelid for PA signal detection.
Apply ultrasonic gel between the transducer tip and animal eyelid to ensure good acoustic coupling.
Amplify the PA signal using two amplifiers.
Digitize the amplified PA signal using a data acquisition board.
Maximize the frequency-doubling efficiency of the BBO crystal.
Wear LG3 goggles for eye protection when optimizing the PAOM illuminating light.
Collimate the fiber output laser of PAOM to a diameter of 2.0 mm.
Align the combined illumination lights of PAOM and SD-OCT to be coaxial.
Set the PAOM excitation light at ~40 nJ/pulse.
Set the SD-OCT probing light at ~0.8 mW.
Transfer the rat to a transparent polypropylene box.
Anesthetize the animal with a mixture of isoflurane and normal air at 1.5% concentration and 2.0 liter/min flow rate for 10 min.
Restrain the anesthetized rat in a homemade holder with five-axis adjustable freedom.
Keep the body temperature of the restrained rat at ~37 °C using a heating pad.
Maintain anesthesia by inhalation gas of mixed isoflurane and normal air with 1.0% concentration and 1.5 liter/min flow rate throughout the experiment.
Cut the eyelash using a surgical scissors.
Dilate the pupils with 1% Tropicamide ophthalmic solution.
Paralyze the iris sphincter muscle using 0.5% Tetracaine Hydrochloride ophthalmic solution.
Apply artificial tear drops to the rat eye every other minute.
Monitor the animal heart rate, respiration, and blood oxygenation by a pulse oximeter.
Turn on SD-OCT illuminating light.
Check the probing light intensity to be ~0.8 mW.
Activate the galvanometer scanning.
Align the SD-OCT irradiation light delivery onto the rat retina.
Identify the retinal region of interest (ROI) by adjusting the five-axis animal holder.
Place the optic disc in the center of the field of view.
Optimize the SD-OCT imaging qualities of retinal cross section in both scanning directions.
Switch the raster scanning direction to reach the best optical focus.
Prepare the needle transducer on a five-axis adjustable platform.
Apply a drop of ultrasonic gel to the transducer tip.
Gently contact the transducer tip to the animal eyelid.
Set PAOM laser to external-trigger mode.
Start the galvanometer scanning.
Activate real-time display of PAOM cross-sectional image of the animal retina.
Carefully adjust the transducer orientation until the PAOM image has the best signal-to-noise ratio.
Ensure an evenly distributed PA amplitude pattern in both scanning directions.
Set the scanning parameters.
Conduct simultaneous retinal imaging of SD-OCT and PAOM.
Reconstruct three-dimensional images of SD-OCT off-line.
Reconstruct three-dimensional images of PAOM off-line.
Remove the animal from the holder immediately after experiment.
Keep the animal warm until it wakes up naturally.
Keep the animal in a dark environment for an extra hour for eyes to recover.
